**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

The Agreement imposes no non-solicitation, no-hire, or anti-poaching restriction on Corio, which is exactly our playbook's preferred position ("No non-solicit on Customer").

What I checked and ruled out:
- **§13 Shared Resources** — the most likely home for such a covenant, since §§13.1–13.3 second Commerce One operations, consulting, and engineering personnel to work alongside Corio staff. Despite that personnel intermingling, the section contains only confidentiality/invention-assignment warranties (p0116), with no hiring restriction.
- **§14 Miscellaneous** — read in full; §14.5 (p0126) is a routine independent-contractor disclaimer, not a restrictive covenant.
- **§10 Confidentiality** — pure Confidential Information use restriction, no personnel covenant.
- **Exhibit D ¶5 "Personnel"** (p0203) — only requires each party to dedicate a sales/marketing employee to joint promotion.
- Literal and regex searches for "solicit", "hire", "recruit", "induce", and "shall not (solicit|hire|employ|recruit|induce)" returned zero hits; "employ" appears only in the unrelated contexts above.

Worth noting for negotiation posture: because Commerce One is embedding its personnel with Corio's team under §13, Commerce One may later request a mutual non-solicit. If it surfaces, our fallback applies — personnel directly involved in the services, 12 months from end of involvement, carve-outs for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches, and no "no-hire."
